title: Enterprise onboarding, escalation, integration & QBR playbook
author: Marco Reyes
summary: Comprehensive playbook combining enterprise onboarding steps, integration checklist, escalation procedures, known issues & workarounds, support process, and QBR / health-check templates for Customer Success and Support teams.
body:
Purpose:
This document is the canonical playbook for onboarding enterprise customers onto Redwood Inference, handling escalations, integrating with customers' environments, running recurring health checks, and preparing Quarterly Business Reviews (QBRs). It consolidates runbooks, checklists, SLOs, escalation matrices, and sample artifacts used by Customer Success, Support, and Solutions Engineering.

Scope and audience:
- Scope: Hosted, Dedicated, and Private (VPC / on-prem) enterprise customers during onboarding and the first 12 months of production.
- Audience: Customer Success Managers (CSMs), Technical Account Managers (TAMs), Support Engineers, Solutions Engineers, SRE on-call, and Sales Engineers.

Owners and escalation contacts:
- Document owner: Marco Reyes (Customer Success)
- On-call / escalation owner: Eng SRE Team (see on-call roster)
- Primary TAM contact: assigned per-account (link to rota)

Key objectives:
- Ensure safe, secure, and timely onboarding with measurable milestones.
- Minimize time-to-first-successful-inference (TTFSI) for production workloads.
- Provide clear escalation paths with SLAs and playbook steps.
- Capture known issues & workarounds to accelerate resolution.
- Deliver actionable health checks and QBR artifacts that demonstrate value and stability.

1) Enterprise onboarding playbook (phased approach)
Overview: The onboarding program is organized into four phases: Kickoff, Integration & Validation, Pilot and Performance Tuning, Production Rollout & Handover. Each phase has owners, acceptance criteria, and exit checks.

Phase A — Kickoff (Week 0)
- Goals: align stakeholders, collect contact information, define success criteria and timeline.
- Deliverables: signed onboarding plan, designated TAM and engineering owners, SSO/SCIM requirements, security questionnaire.
- Checklist:
  1. Schedule kickoff meeting with customer stakeholders (product, infra, security).
  2. Share onboarding plan and milestones (GANTT or calendar invites).
  3. Confirm contractual requirements (data residency, compliance add-ons).
  4. Collect API key scope requirements and initial traffic profile (RPS, token volume).

Phase B — Integration & Validation (Week 1–3)
- Goals: complete authentication, network connectivity, and sample integration.
- Deliverables: successful authentication (API/SSO), validated request/response cycle, basic observability dashboards.
- Checklist:
  1. Network: validate IP allowlist, VPN/VPC peering, or private endpoint configuration.
  2. Authentication: configure API key or OIDC/SSO + test tokens.
  3. SDKs & quickstarts: run SDK quickstart (Node/Python) and verify sample generation.
  4. Logging and metrics: ensure logs forwarded to customer (if required) and per-route metrics visible in Console.
  5. Security: verify KMS/HSM integration and encryption-at-rest configuration (Private deployments).

Phase C — Pilot & Performance Tuning (Week 3–6)
- Goals: validate throughput and latency against SLOs, tune batching, and KV cache.
- Deliverables: pilot runbook, performance profile, recommended model/quantization config.
- Checklist:
  1. Establish test dataset and representative traffic pattern.
  2. Run load tests to target RPS and peak traffic.
  3. Tune batching parameters and caching TTLs.
  4. Record baseline cost per 1k tokens and latency percentiles (p50/p95/p99).
  5. Approve model variant and rollout policy for production.

Phase D — Production Rollout & Handover (Week 6+)
- Goals: cutover to production, confirm post-cutover monitoring, and hand over to CS Ops/Support.
- Deliverables: production runbook, SLA expectations, documentation handoff, QBR cadence set.
- Checklist:
  1. Execute canary or phased rollout per rollout policy.
  2. Validate SLOs for 72 hours post-cutover (latency, error rate, availability).
  3. Complete knowledge transfer sessions with Support and SRE on-call.
  4. Schedule first 30/60/90-day health checks and QBR cadence.

2) Integration guide (technical checklist and sample configs)
Prerequisites:
- Customer network architecture diagram.
- API key or OIDC provider details.
- List of models and expected request patterns.

Minimum configuration items (table):
| Item | Required | Notes |
|---|---:|---|
| IP allowlist / Private Endpoint | Yes (for private deployments) | Provide CIDR and test connectivity steps |
| API auth (API key or OIDC) | Yes | Recommend OIDC for SSO + short-lived tokens |
| TLS | Yes | TLS 1.2+ enforced |
| KMS/HSM | Conditional | Required for regulated customers (HIPAA/PAYMENTS) |
| Logging integration | Recommended | Forward structured logs to customer SIEM if requested |

Sample curl to validate generation:
curl -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate -H "Authorization: Bearer <API_KEY>" -H "Content-Type: application/json" --data '{"model":"redwood-large-1","input":"Say hello"}'

Network validation steps (numbered):
1. From a host in customer environment, curl the health endpoint and confirm 200.
2. Trace route to private endpoint and validate connection via VPN/Tunnel.
3. If using Dedicated, confirm TLS certificate CN and CA chain match customer policy.

3) Escalation playbook (severity mapping and steps)
Severity definitions and target SLAs:
- Sev 1 (Critical): production outage affecting >50% of requests or data loss. Target response: 15 min, mitigation in 1 hour.
- Sev 2 (High): significant degradation (latency > 2x SLO or errors affecting key routes). Target response: 30 min, mitigation in 4 hours.
- Sev 3 (Medium): partial feature impact, limited customer workarounds. Target response: 4 hours, mitigation in 2 business days.
- Sev 4 (Low): general questions, feature requests. Target response: 1 business day.

Escalation steps (for Sev 1/2):
1. Triage: Support engineer reproduces issue and collects logs, sample request IDs, and timestamps.
2. Notify: open incident in PagerDuty, tag on-call SRE and TAM.
3. Contain: if a model variant is causing the issue, immediate fallback to previous approved variant per rollback policy.
4. Mitigate: apply rate-limits, scale Dedicated pool, or enable degraded-mode routing to hosted endpoints.
5. Root Cause Analysis (RCA): create postmortem within 72 hours for Sev 1, 7 days for Sev 2.

Escalation matrix (contacts):
- Support Tier 1: Support Engineers (support@redwood.ai) — initial triage.
- Support Tier 2: Solutions Engineering — deep-dive, reproducibility.
- Support Tier 3: Eng SRE and Runtime Team — kernel-level or infra issues.
- Exec escalation: Head of Support and CSM Director for customer-impacting outages.

4) Support process and ticket lifecycle
Ticket intake channels:
- Customer portal (preferred)
- Email: support@redwood.ai
- In-app / Console reports
- PagerDuty for Sev 1 incidents

Ticket flow (numbered):
1. Intake: create ticket with customer, environment, severity, and sample request IDs.
2. Acknowledge: Tier 1 acknowledges within the SLA.
3. Triage & reproduce: gather logs, traces, and reproduce in staging if possible.
4. Escalate: follow escalation playbook if beyond Tier 1.
5. Resolution & validation: confirm fix with customer and close after 24-hour validation window for production fixes.
6. Post-incident review: for Sev1/2 run RCA and TL;DR for the customer; capture follow-ups as JIRA tickets.

SLA mapping (summary):
- Sev 1: initial response 15 min, update cadence 15 min until mitigation.
- Sev 2: initial response 30 min, update cadence 60 min until mitigation.
- Sev 3: initial response 4 hours, update cadence daily until resolved.
- Sev 4: initial response 1 business day.

5) Known issues & common workarounds (living list)
- Issue KS-203: Intermittent p99 spikes on long-context prompts
  - Symptoms: p99 latency spikes during sustained long-context requests (>4k tokens) on Dedicated pools.
  - Workaround: reduce request parallelism, increase batch-window to 25ms, enable KV prefix caching for repeated prefixes.
  - Status: mitigated via tuning; engineering action item: improved kernel scheduling (ENG-1209).

- Issue KS-306: OIDC token expiry causing 401s after 1 hour for some SSO providers
  - Symptoms: periodic 401s at token expiry during long-running sessions.
  - Workaround: implement refresh token flow with short-lived access tokens; set token refresh at t-300s from expiry.
  - Status: documented; support KB created.

- Issue KS-410: Bulk-embedding requests time out at scale for very large payloads
  - Symptoms: 504 gateway timeout on requests >10k items in single batch.
  - Workaround: split bulk requests into smaller batches (<=2000 items) and increase client timeout to 120s.
  - Status: queued for SDK change to auto-chunk (SE-77).

How to contribute a known issue:
1. Create an internal ticket with reproduction steps and request IDs.
2. Tag with label "known-issue" and include workaround.
3. Reviewer (Solutions Engineering) validates and promotes to the living list.

6) Health checks and QBR templates
Health check cadence and checklist:
- 30-day: connectivity, auth, basic SLO validation (p50/p95), error rates, and billing spike review.
- 60-day: performance tuning review, batching and cache efficiency, cost per 1k tokens.
- 90-day: platform upgrades, model variant review, and business KPIs achieved.

Standard health-check items (bulleted):
- Uptime last 30/90 days (target 99.9% for Dedicated + hosted fallbacks).
- Latency percentiles by route (p50/p95/p99).
- Error rate by category (4xx vs 5xx) and top error signatures.
- Token consumption trends and cost anomaly detection.
- Security: successful auth checks, no audit log anomalies.

QBR template (agenda items):
1. Attendees and objectives (5 min)
2. Executive summary (impact, uptime, major incidents) (10 min)
3. Usage & cost trends (tokens, embeddings, unit economics) (15 min)
4. Performance & reliability (SLOs, p95/p99, incidents) (15 min)
5. Roadmap & upcoming changes (model upgrades, Private deployments) (10 min)
6. Action items & ownership (10 min)
7. Open discussion and next steps (15 min)

Deliverables for QBR:
- QBR slide deck (share PDF) with KPIs, incident summary, and recommended optimizations.
- Runbook updates for any recurring issues.
- Follow-up TODOs tracked in joint project board.

7) Attachments and templates (links)
- Onboarding checklist (spreadsheet link)
- Sample QBR slide deck (template)
- Network validation playbook (CLI snippets)
- RCA template (postmortem template)

8) Metrics and dashboards (what to track)
- Per-route RPS, concurrency, and token throughput.
- Latency histograms and p95/p99 trends.
- Error budget burn rate and SLO alerts.
- Cost per 1k tokens and estimated monthly spend.

9) Operational notes and handover checklist
- Support must have access to customer logs and example request IDs.
- SRE must be invited to first cutover for production verification.
- TAM to schedule 30/60/90-day check-ins and QBR cadence.

10) Appendix: quick troubleshooting cheatsheet
- If customer sees 401s: verify API key / OIDC config and system clocks (NTP drift).
- If latency spikes: check batch-window, KV cache hit-rate, and model variant.
- If errors increase post-deploy: rollback to previous model variant and open a P0 investigation.

Revision history:
- 2026-09-15: Document created by Marco Reyes (initial consolidated playbook).
- 2026-10-05: Reviewed and updated escalation SLAs, added known issues KS-410 and updated QBR template (reviewers: Emily Chen, Rakesh Singh, Leah Morrison).

Notes and next steps:
- Keep this document synchronized with the Support KB and Solutions Engineering runbooks.
- Quarterly review required to capture new known issues and update SLOs.

For questions or additions, contact the document owner or the Customer Success Slack channel (#cs-enterprise).
